A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same A2GC research work. All pages, equations, eight tables and four figures support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original A2GC retrieval experiments, component and configuration ablations, latency measurements, and generalization tests in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds configuration-specific benchmark results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The asymmetric normalization and marginal calibration procedure, geometric embeddings, score fusion, backbone integration and descriptor construction remain unchanged. Figure 2 is restyled without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSV-Cities training and retain Pittsburgh, MSLS, Nordland spring-versus-winter, SPED and SF-XL evaluations. The shortened dataset headings in Table 1 do not introduce different coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains identical in Table 1, the Nordland/SPED comparison, the SF-XL comparison and the qualitative examples. New descriptor-size and reranking annotations describe existing comparators rather than adding or replacing methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same training settings, preprocessing, evaluation metrics and retrieval procedure. The additional Table 1 results use backbone and descriptor choices already documented in v1's Tables 2–3; no revised split, budget or testing procedure is stated.

E4.justification: The backbone, descriptor-size, fine-tuning, component-removal and resolution ablations in Tables 2–6 are unchanged, as are the generalization tests and qualitative analyses. Table 1 adds benchmark scores without introducing a new ablation or robustness question.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice and qualitative feature-matching statistics remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds ViTb rows with descriptor sizes 2112, 8448 and 33280. Their Pitts30k scores already appeared in Table 3, but their Pitts250k and MSLS scores are newly reported; for example, the 8448-dimensional configuration gives 93.3/97.4/97.9 on MSLS-V. All pre-existing table scores, including the original A2GC row now labeled 33280 (ViTg), remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The optimal-transport formulation, assumptions, normalization equations and geometric definitions in Equations 1–12 are unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about asymmetric aggregation, geometric constraints, retrieval performance and cross-domain generalization. The added results do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning complementary components, possible overfitting, accuracy–computation tradeoffs and viewpoint-invariant attention are retained. No substantive limitation, applicability boundary or explanation of the new Table 1 results is added.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly discloses descriptor dimensions, selected backbone identities and labels identifying two-stage reranking comparators. It also identifies the previously unspecified main A2GC row as 33280-dimensional ViTg. Implementation details, hardware and the code-access link otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 24 works and retain the same related-work discussion and novelty positioning. Reference formatting and citation-page changes do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits, including reordered phrasing in Section 3.2.2, revised table captions and shortened benchmark labels. Section order and the substantive narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a descriptor-size column, reranking markers, three A2GC rows and shaded highlighting. Figure 2 is restyled, Figures 1 and 3 are resized, and surrounding material reflows. Existing figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded Table 1 improves comparison transparency by identifying configurations and providing additional results for smaller A2GC descriptors. These are useful, limited gains rather than improved best scores or a methodological advance. Documentation remains incomplete: the new 8448-dimensional ViTb MSLS-V Recall@1 of 93.3 is not reconciled with Table 6's 90.4 for 224-pixel ViTb evaluation, so equivalence of those settings cannot be established.
